title: Predictive signal ingestion + forecast provider interface for Dedicated autoscaler
creator: Vanessa Ortiz
project: Autoscaling policies with customer bounds (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
description:
Context
Dedicated autoscaling currently uses reactive signals (saturation, queue depth, operator overrides). For enterprise customers with predictable ramps, we want an optional “predictive mode” that biases scale decisions using demand forecasts while still respecting hard min/max bounds.

Scope of this ticket
Implement the ingestion path + provider interface for forecast inputs, including:
- Forecast provider interface (contract + runtime adapter)
- Staleness checks and validation (don’t use stale/partial data)
- Feature flag gating (per account/deployment + kill switch)
- Fallback behavior to reactive scaling when forecasts are missing/invalid
- Telemetry for forecast quality + fallback reasons (for dashboards/alerts)

Non-goals
- Improving the predictive model/forecasting algorithm itself (handled by prediction service owners)
- Cross-region placement optimization
- Procurement automation

Requirements / semantics
1) Provider interface
- Autoscaler consumes an interface that returns a recommended desired_replica_count (or desired_capacity_units) per deployment_id, per region.
- Must support returning: forecasted demand over a horizon (default 60 min), lead time (default 10 min), and confidence.
- API must be non-blocking for autoscaler loop; enforce a strict timeout and use cached last-good forecast where appropriate.

2) Staleness + validity
- A forecast is considered valid if:
  - forecast.generated_at is within max_age_seconds (default 600s / 10m)
  - horizon_seconds >= configured horizon (default 3600s / 60m)
  - includes region match for the deployment’s region
  - confidence is present (even if low)
- If stale/invalid: do NOT apply predictive bias. Emit a fallback reason and continue with reactive.

3) Feature flag
- Gate predictive mode behind:
  - Account-level flag: dedicated_predictive_autoscaling
  - Deployment-level flag / policy toggle: scaling_policy.predictive_mode = enabled
- Include an emergency kill switch (global) to force reactive-only behavior without needing config edits.

4) Fallback + arbitration (high-level; detailed precedence defined in ADR)
- If forecast unavailable/invalid/stale OR provider errors/timeout: reactive-only.
- If reactive indicates immediate overload (queue depth / saturation over threshold): reactive dominates (but still respect bounds).
- Otherwise: predictive bias can increase desired capacity early (bias up), but should not force scale-down below reactive unless explicitly allowed by policy (initially: do NOT bias down; only bias up).

5) Observability
Emit structured logs + metrics to support dashboards and auditability:
- requested_desired_replicas (reactive)
- forecast_desired_replicas
- forecast_age_seconds
- predictive_applied (true/false)
- predictive_fallback_reason (enum)
- bounded_desired_replicas (post min/max clamp; emitted elsewhere but referenced here)
- prediction_error metrics are tracked in ENG-22143, but this ticket should emit the primitives needed to compute error.

Design/links
- Confluence architecture: sources/confluence/eng-infra/gpu-fleet-and-capacity/autoscaler-bounds-and-predictive-signals-architecture.json
- ADR (precedence + invariants): sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-autoscaling-bounds-precedence-and-safety-invariants.json

Acceptance criteria
- Autoscaler can call a ForecastSignalProvider (mock + real adapter) and incorporate results behind feature flags.
- Staleness checks implemented with default max_age_seconds=600 and hard timeout <= 150ms per autoscaler loop (configurable).
- Clear fallback behavior implemented and covered by tests:
  - provider timeout
  - provider returns null / empty
  - stale forecast
  - forecast for wrong region
  - low confidence (still valid but logged)
- Telemetry includes fallback reason and forecast age.
- Rollout plan documented in ticket (pilot accounts only; kill switch verified).

Implementation notes (proposal)
- Define interface in autoscaler module:
  - GetForecast(deployment_id, region, now) -> {desired_replicas, generated_at, horizon_seconds, lead_time_seconds, confidence, source}
- Adapter implementation:
  - HTTP/gRPC client to prediction service (name TBD; likely capacity-forecasting)
  - Cache last-good forecast per (deployment_id, region) for <= 10m
  - Enforce request deadline and circuit-break on repeated failures
- Fallback reasons enum:
  - disabled_by_flag
  - policy_disabled
  - provider_timeout
  - provider_error
  - forecast_missing
  - forecast_stale
  - forecast_invalid
  - overload_reactive_override

Test plan
- Unit tests:
  - validation/staleness logic
  - caching and last-good behavior
  - feature flag gating matrix
- Integration tests:
  - fake forecast service with controllable timestamps
- Canary:
  - enable for one pilot deployment in us-east with synthetic daily ramp

Risks / open questions
- What is the correct lead time for GPU provisioning in Dedicated (10m default may be too low for some SKUs/regions). Need to confirm with Jamal + fleet provisioning metrics.
- Forecast service SLA and rate limits: autoscaler calls must not overload it; caching and batching may be needed.
- Timezone alignment: forecast timestamps must be UTC; validate explicitly.

Owners
- DRI: Mei Lin
- Reviewers: Keiko Yamamoto, Vanessa Ortiz, Rafael Mendes
comments: 2025-06-10 — Vanessa Ortiz: Creating ticket to unblock predictive-mode integration. Please keep provider interface minimal; we can iterate once we have pilot feedback. Hard requirement: staleness + safe fallback, no surprises.

2025-06-13 — Mei Lin: Drafted provider contract proposal (desired_replicas + generated_at + horizon + lead_time + confidence). Suggest bias-up only for v1 to avoid oscillation risk. Need confirmation from autoscaler owners.
2025-06-17 — Keiko Yamamoto: +1 bias-up only. Also please ensure provider call is out of the hot path (cache, deadline). Autoscaler loop budget is tight during bursty workloads.

2025-06-20 — Rafael Mendes: From SRE side: please add explicit fallback_reason values and a metric for forecast_age_seconds. We need to page on “predictive enabled but stale for > N mins” only during pilot, otherwise it’ll be noisy.

2025-06-27 — Mei Lin: Implemented interface + stub adapter behind account flag. Added validation for region match + horizon. Default max_age=10m, timeout=150ms. Next: wire to real forecast endpoint and add circuit breaker.

2025-07-03 — Mei Lin: Wired adapter to capacity-forecasting service in staging. Added cache (last-good per deployment/region). If forecast missing/stale: reactive-only + logs fallback_reason. Starting integration tests now.

2025-07-11 — Keiko Yamamoto: Code review notes: ensure null forecast can’t cause scale-to-zero; clamp forecast_desired_replicas to >= 0 but do not apply if missing. Also prefer emitting “predictive_applied=false” rather than omitting metrics.

2025-07-18 — Mei Lin: Addressed review feedback. Added guard: if provider returns null/empty -> fallback_reason=forecast_missing and predictive_applied=false. Added metrics emission in all branches. Ready for second review.
2025-07-25 — Vanessa Ortiz: Marking In Review pending final sign-off from SRE on telemetry naming. Please link PR and confirm kill switch behavior in staging before pilot enablement.
